text: The paper reports that with 6 revealed pixels, debate with precommit turns a judge that is 59.4% accurate on random pixels into a debate in which the judge is correct on 88.9% of MNIST test images, and with 4 pixels 48.2% becomes 85.2%. The authors state precommit is crucial for both pixel budgets because the liar does much better when the lie can adapt across the game tree; without the mean-over-3-seeds adjustment the honest player wins 87.7% (6 pixels) and 83.8% (4 pixels).
title: MNIST debate with precommit: judge accuracy 59.4% to 88.9% (6 px), 48.2% to 85.2% (4 px)
